name: 46,XY Difference of Sex Development Due to Testicular 17,20-Desmolase Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Biochemical Diagnostic Criteria for 17,20-Desmolase Deficiency

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in the CYP17A1 gene affecting 17,20-lyase activity
Elevated 17-hydroxypregnenolone and 17-hydroxyprogesterone with low or absent androgens (androstenedione, testosterone)
Presence of undervirilized external genitalia in 46,XY individuals with normal Müllerian structures absent
Detection of testes in typical location without Müllerian derivatives on imaging
Blunted or absent androgen response after human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) stimulation test

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic CYP17A1 variants plus characteristic biochemical profile and clinical presentation of undervirilization in 46,XY individuals
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Differentiation from combined 17α-hydroxylase/17,20-lyase deficiency is critical; isolated 17,20-lyase deficiency spares cortisol synthesis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ambiguous or undervirilized external genitalia in 46,XY individuals
pathognomonic.notes: Includes micropenis, hypospadias, and bifid scrotum

pathognomonic.symptomName: Normal female internal Müllerian structures absent
pathognomonic.notes: Differentiates from other DSDs with Müllerian persistence
searchTerms: missing normal female internal reproductive organs
late or missing male puberty changes

common.notes: Resulting from altered androgen to estrogen ratio
searchTerms: breast tissue growth in teenage boys

common.symptomName: Normal cortisol production without adrenal insufficiency
common.notes: Distinguishes isolated 17,20-lyase deficiency from combined deficiency
Undescended testes common in affected individuals

occasional.notes: Rarely reported due to mild mineralocorticoid excess

occasional.symptomName: Osteopenia or decreased bone mineral density

occasional.notes: Occasionally observed due to altered steroidogenesis

rare.notes: Mild adrenal enlargement may be seen on imaging

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric manifestations such as anxiety or depression
rare.notes: Likely secondary to chronic hormonal imbalance
Rarely reported due to mild ACTH elevation

imaging: Ultrasound or MRI showing testes in scrotal or inguinal position
other: Blunted androgen response to hCG stimulation test

distinguishingFeatures: Impaired cortisol synthesis with adrenal insufficiency
Presence of female external genitalia despite 46,XY karyotype

redFlags: Severe undervirilization of external genitalia in 46,XY neonate
Failure to virilize at puberty despite normal cortisol levels
references: Miller WL. Disorders in the initial steps of steroid hormone synthesis. J Steroid Biochem Mol Biol. 2017;165(Pt A):18-37.
Auchus RJ. The genetics, pathophysiology, and management of isolated 17,20-lyase deficiency. Endocrinol Metab Clin North Am. 2011;40(2):361-374.
